goal: Map the current landscape of AI agents in scientific workflows for a discussion with DOE x-ray and neutron facility scientists, delivered as a self-contained HTML report with an appendix and verified references

iterations.thought: Bootstrap. The done_when proof runs on the network, so I first built a shared rate-limited lookup helper in the scratchpad (a file lock per service keeps arXiv at >=3.1 s between requests across all concurrent agents) and a python->python3.12 shim, because the host has no 'python' on PATH. Decomposed into five disjoint research lanes, one per question area Q1-Q5 (Q6 is a synthesis written later from their evidence), plus one tooling lane that builds the report generator and an independent checker, so the content and the proof machinery are built in parallel.

delegated.task: Catalog >=38 general-science agent systems by stage x autonomy (L1-L4) with verified refs; taxonomy table, 2024-2026 trends, 'new in 2026'
Separate peer-reviewed / independently validated results from claims (with what would validate each); benchmark table with best scores, dates, human baselines
Models, agent frameworks, MCP/A2A protocols, and how agents connect to workflow/HPC systems (Globus Compute, Parsl, Academy, IRI, Bluesky/EPICS/Tiled)
Agents at DOE x-ray/neutron facilities and labs (steering, data analysis, knowledge assistants), DOE programs via OSTI and DOE pages; >=8 facility catalog rows
Reproducibility, fabricated citations/results, evaluation gaps, safety and dual use, credit and authorship, with a risk register

report/build_report.py + template.html (inline CSS) and independent check_report.py (HTML contract, Crossref/arXiv/URL resolution with title match, external-resource scan) plus a scratchpad fixture test

iterations.thought: Write and harden. Sections are separable once refs and catalog are merged, so five writers turn the lane notes into HTML fragments under a strict contract (one p.answer, qN- subsection ids, canonical [@key] citations) while an adversarial fact-checker attacks ~80 headline numbers against primary sources in parallel. I keep the cross-cutting pieces (Q6 prompts linking to Q1-Q5 anchors, summary, appendix frame, taxonomy generator) so Q6 can only cite evidence that the sections actually contain.

iterations.thought: Verify and harden with the surplus iteration. The iteration-2 audit covered headline numbers only, so the remaining risk is qualitative: sentences whose citation does not say what the text says, catalog labels that overstate autonomy, cross-section contradictions, and jargon this audience cannot parse. Split into three disjoint sentence-level citation audits (Q1+Q3, Q4 alone because the audience reads it most closely, Q5+Q6+summary incl. Q6 link targets), one catalog-label audit, and one reader review limited to wording; each returns exact old->new edits so integration is mechanical and order-controlled (facts first, wording last).
